context: Cycle plot of U.S. monthly retail sales 2020–2024: 12 panels (one per month), each showing 5 data points (one per year) connected by a trend line, with a per-panel dashed mean line, a shared Y-axis, holiday season bracket annotation, COVID dip callout, and a 5-shade blue sequential color scale for years.
first_impression: Clean and immediately readable — the shared Y-axis and sequential blue palette let you scan across all 12 panels without losing orientation.
what_works: The 5-shade sequential blue palette encodes year as a temporal gradient (light=older, dark=newer), making the upward trend across years self-evident without requiring legend lookup; the per-panel dashed mean lines serve as a strong cognitive anchor, letting you instantly judge whether each year is above or below that month's norm.
what_doesnt: The per-panel mean value labels ($89, $92, etc.) are right-edge-anchored and bleed into adjacent panel space, creating clutter especially in mid-chart panels where label text competes with neighboring dots; the 60 tiny year tick labels ('20–'24 × 12 panels) at the bottom form a dense strip that is hard to parse without zooming, undermining the otherwise clean layout.
